title: Adjudicate human neuronal FTMT protein and remove unrestricted CTA eligibility
body:
The 25 October 2026 audit found normal-tissue evidence that conflicts with the current unrestricted CTA assignment for **FTMT** (`ENSG00000181867`). This is an evidence-curation issue, not a request for a symbol-specific classifier exception or a claim of demonstrated therapeutic injury.

Current frozen policy: `oncoref.target-sets.2026-10-24.1`, mapped nomination universe 399 CTA / 561 Neither / 1,580 Unsafe. [Published atlas](https://pirl-unc.github.io/oncoref/audits/cta-atlas-20261024/).

| Recorded quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Current category | CTA / Pass |
| Reproductive bulk RNA | 52.6 nTPM |
| Maximum audited non-permitted RNA, nTPM sources | 7.4 nTPM |
| Maximum audited non-permitted RNA, TPM sources | 0.1458 TPM |
| Highest non-permitted nTPM context | 7.4 nTPM; testis/macrophages; hpa_single_cell_tissue; vital |
| Review completed so far | Primary full text |

The maxima are from separate source-native observations, not matched donor RNA/IHC or interchangeable bulk/cell measurements.

### Evidence

Human substantia nigra neurons contain FTMT protein. The 2017 study used two postmortem donors without neurological disorders, a monoclonal reagent, absorption controls and an H-ferritin cross-reactivity check. The later study includes control as well as hemorrhage cases.

Normal neuronal protein conflicts with unrestricted reproductive targeting, even when bulk brain RNA is low. This is not evidence of an observed FTMT-directed treatment injury.

- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28386150/
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38988693/

### Requested adjudication

Check human versus monkey observations; retain the two neurologically unaffected human donors, antibody absorption and H-ferritin specificity controls. Keep the later control/hemorrhage observations separate from the original study.

Proposed endpoint: **Unsafe after acceptance of the normal-protein evidence; otherwise Neither pending material uncertainty**. If review invalidates the concern, preserve the rejected finding and its reason. The endpoint is conditional on evidence, not a required benchmark answer.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Record exact species/reference/gene or protein-group identity, nonmalignant cell compartment/state, primary source and figure/table, assay and specificity controls, with Accepted/Unresolved/Rejected status and review rationale.
- [ ] Reconcile contradictory source records explicitly; an abstract cannot establish controls it does not report. Do not erase raw evidence or substitute a paralog.
- [ ] Apply the common normal-protein veto or unresolved-conflict hold; no per-gene threshold or whitelist. Accepted normal protein excludes even when bulk RNA passes.
- [ ] Rebuild the gene decision and affected complete-protein/k-mer background under a versioned policy; preserve every reason and the existing distinction between Neither and forbidden proteins.
- [ ] Publish the evidence and category delta with a regression case that exercises the general rule. Distinguish normal expression from observed clinical toxicity.

title: Reconcile primary normal-antibody signals for 180 retained CTA assignments
body:
The 25 October literature/source audit found 1,707 positive primary-antibody normal-compartment rows across **180 currently retained gene assignments**. Of these, 103 assignments have Medium/High primary staining in Vital compartments; 78 have at least one profile note explicitly mentioning off-target/cross-reactivity or nonspecificity. These are not independent proteins, donors or proven injuries, and shared family reagents can repeat across genes.

The current normal-cell report deliberately permits curated negative HPA profiles to supersede primary staining. This is appropriate for documented nonspecific signals, but leaves credible unresolved conflicts without an explicit, source-specific decision. A global antibody reliability label cannot settle every tissue stain.

Reproduce from the pinned `docs/audits/cta-normal-cells-20261023/primary-antibodies.csv.gz`, selecting `normal_signal` rows for the 399 CTA IDs in `docs/audits/cta-atlas-20261024/all-genes.csv`. Input SHA256 values are `f5a37339a5d12e844f97ff18ff6ba28f98fa3cacd021ac89a3780cef5467f413` and `dff2c194404281cedfd6ddaf86505b0b02faeacd645506e5cf8fde774a74d09d`, respectively. The derived local audit is `docs/audits/cta-literature-20261025/retained-primary-normal-signals.csv` (not yet a published artifact).

### Required behavior

- Accepted endogenous protein in non-permitted normal cells -> Unsafe, even if RNA is low.
- Credible unresolved identity/specificity/context -> Neither with an explicit review task.
- Specifically adjudicated off-target staining -> rejected finding retained in provenance; no automatic veto.
- Missing or merely unreviewed search results -> no invented protein positive or negative.

Do not automatically exclude all 180. Do not use a regex warning as an automatic rejection of every antibody for a gene. SAGE1 profiles explicitly report disregarded presumed off-target binding; YBX2 has multiple discordant primary records without that same explanation. MAGEA4 and PRAME clinical experience is product-specific and cannot settle all raw stains by itself.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Deduplicate shared reagent, source and donor lineage; retain family/gene attribution uncertainty.
- [ ] Record a per-finding Accepted/Unresolved/Rejected status, specific rationale, source image/annotation and scope; preserve curated and raw observations.
- [ ] Prioritize the 103 Vital Medium/High assignments, then remaining compartments; report reviewed and unresolved denominators separately.
- [ ] Use the common rules in #627, without gene-specific thresholds. Reproductive controls and local negatives only relax their validated contexts.
- [ ] Test specific-positive/curated-negative conflicts, documented off-target rejection, duplicate family rows, missing staining and paired versus unpaired donor contexts.
- [ ] Publish all gene/protein changes and review records before changing released target/forbidden exports.

title: Measure continuous normal-expression breadth without rescue by a reproductive maximum
body:
The current tissue-by-tissue reproductive maximum can make a broadly expressed gene look selective when one reproductive compartment is high. Add an independent, continuous description of the normal expression profile. This should not count tissues above an arbitrary detection threshold or silently pool incomparable datasets.

### Proposed descriptive measure

For each comparable study and category, use:

`B = sum_j w_j * x_j / (x_j + L_j)`

`x_j` is a prespecified donor summary for a normal compartment; `L_j` is that assay/context's applicable ceiling; fixed anatomical weights sum to one. Begin with the bulk sources for which the existing ceilings are defined. Cell data need their own documented calibration. Report median and upper-quantile versions separately when independent donor counts support them.

Compute Vital, Protected and Manageable values separately. This is an expression burden relative to research ceilings, not injury probability or a reproductive fraction. It must rise with normal expression and must not improve merely because reproductive RNA rises. Accepted focal normal protein and hard RNA vetoes retain precedence.

### Coverage and uncertainty

- Fixed, non-overlapping anatomy and within-organ weights: adding redundant brain subregions or an atlas copy must not change the score through representation count alone.
- Preserve observed weighted contribution and missing weight. Missing compartments contribute an explicit possible interval `[0, missing_weight]`; do not renormalize only over favorable observed tissues.
- Separate the missing-coverage range from sampling confidence intervals. Resample independent donors where supported; no invented intervals from one summary value or pooled cells.
- Do not mix TPM, nTPM and CP10K or import human ceilings to another species. Keep cohort overlap and platform shifts explicit.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Publish per-gene full profiles, source-specific burdens, donor quantiles/counts, coverage ranges and sensitivity to reasonable anatomical weighting.
- [ ] Compare diffuse cases such as ZNF730 with established CTA benchmarks and ordinary normal genes; keep their identities out of rule code.
- [ ] Validate any proposed classification cutoff on prespecified biological controls and evaluate held-out genes/families; report all gains/losses, not only preservation of requested CTAs.
- [ ] Initially expose the score for review priority. Do not change memberships or claim a validated numerical cutoff in this issue's first descriptive release.
- [ ] If an admission gate is subsequently approved, diffuse but below-ceiling expression yields Neither; decisive normal protein/RNA still yields Unsafe.
- [ ] Test monotonicity, duplicate-study invariance, compartment splitting with conserved weight, missing coverage, native units and inability of a reproductive peak to erase normal evidence.

title: Complete individual CTA literature adjudication beyond the 32-gene initial review
body:
The 25 October audit searched all **2,540 mapped nominations** using **6,013 queries**, retrieving **36,964 unique paper leads** (41,980 gene-paper pairs). It did **not** complete individual primary-paper adjudication for every gene: 32 genes received new primary-paper assessments, and 46 have specific notes including carried-forward/source reviews. **2,508 genes still lack a new individual primary-paper assessment.** There were 1,688 truncated queries and 160 genes with no hits in either topic search.

The local reproducible artifacts are `docs/audits/cta-literature-20261025/` and `scripts/audit_cta_literature.py`, `scripts/fetch_cta_review_papers.py`, `scripts/build_cta_literature_audit.py`; these files are saved locally but not yet published as a repository commit/release. Search scope, query cutoff, cache hashes and review depth are recorded. Preserve the distinction between retrieval and adjudication.

### Work

1. Publish/review the scripts and pinned audit tables so the paper trail is available beyond the local workspace; preserve raw-response provenance and avoid publishing full copyrighted abstracts unnecessarily.
2. Review every mapped gene individually under the common evidence rules, starting with retained normal-protein conflicts and primary-antibody discrepancies. Resolve aliases, paralogs, species, isoforms, endogenous versus engineered expression, nonmalignant context and independent-source lineage.
3. Expand truncated searches and follow older citations where needed. MRP8/S100A8 versus ABCC11 is a concrete alias collision; family evidence cannot be assigned blindly to each current locus.
4. Review over-exclusions as well as retained concerns: ROPN1 near 30; TDRD1/BRDT modest immune signals; HORMAD1/DAZL repeated immune RNA; ACRBP/TEX101 multiple >30 observations; FOXR2/XAGE5 antibody questions; CTAG2 donor variability. Valid >30 values remain exclusions pending accepted source correction, not a favorable threshold adjustment.
5. Keep tumor occurrence, presented peptide, biological function, treatment efficacy and observed toxicity as separate findings. A published CTA name or participation in a trial does not override normal expression. The gene-level expression screen must not silently certify all peptides/products.

### Completion criteria

- [ ] Every gene has an explicit, source-backed assessment or a clearly reasoned unassessed/unavailable status; no-hit searches do not establish absence or safety.
- [ ] Record exact papers, reviewed portions (abstract/full text), important controls, contradictory findings and the evidence needed for reconsideration. Do not label a lead as a reviewed clinical outcome.
- [ ] Publish all proposed changes, threshold-boundary cases and retained concerns; preserve original and proposed memberships separately until a reviewed versioned rebuild.
